items.title: Netanyahu orders intensified strikes on Hezbollah in Lebanon

featured_image.name: Israeli prime minister orders strikes on Hezbollah targets in Lebanon

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday ordered a further escalation of military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, vowing to "crush" the Iran-backed group amid ongoing drone attacks on Israeli positions despite a ceasefire that has been in effect since April.

"I have ordered an even greater acceleration of our operations," Netanyahu said in a video statement posted on his Telegram channel. "We will intensify our blows, increase our firepower, and we will crush them."[1][2]

The Israeli military responded by launching strikes across the Bekaa Valley in eastern Lebanon and targeting towns in the south, killing at least three people, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strikes followed Israeli evacuation orders for 10 villages, with military spokesman Colonel Avichay Adraee accusing Hezbollah of breaching the truce.[2]

items.title: Iran votes to restore internet after 87-day blackout

featured_image.name: Iran expands tiered internet access amid continued online blackout

items.description: The Iranian government on Monday approved a decision to restore nationwide internet access after a blackout lasting nearly three months, according to the Fars news agency. The vote by the country's Cyberspace Regulation Committee passed with nine members in favor and three opposed, marking a potential turning point in what has become one of the longest government-imposed internet shutdowns ever recorded.[1]

items.title: Iran would reopen Strait of Hormuz 30 days after deal, Nikkei reports

featured_image.name: Trump: Iran deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz 'largely negotiated'

items.description:
Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz approximately 30 days after reaching an agreement with the United States to end hostilities, Japan's Nikkei 225 newspaper reported on Monday, citing a Middle East diplomatic source. Under the reported plan, Iran would clear mines from the strategic waterway during the 30-day post-agreement window, after which ships from all countries would navigate freely, with Tehran also ceasing its collection of transit fees.[1][2]

The report adds that the ceasefire agreed in early April would be extended for 60 days, during which talks on Iran's nuclear program would be held.[1]

items.title: Lavrov urges Rubio to evacuate US embassy from Kyiv

featured_image.name: US Embassy in Kyiv closed as 'potential significant air attack' looms

items.description:
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov called US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Monday to urge the evacuation of American diplomats from Kyiv, delivering a warning that Russian forces plan to launch "systematic and consistent strikes" on the Ukrainian capital, including against "decision-making centers" and military-industrial facilities.[1][2][3]

The phone call, confirmed by Russia's foreign ministry, came as Moscow issued a broader public warning to all foreign nationals, diplomats, and international organizations to leave Kyiv immediately. There was no immediate comment from the US State Department.[4][3][1]

items.title: Carney calls Alberta separation vote a 'dangerous bluff,' cites Brexit experience

featured_image.name: Carney Warns of 'Dangerous Bluff' in Alberta Vote, Citing Brexit

items.description:
Prime Minister Mark Carney warned Monday that Alberta's planned referendum on separation is a "dangerous bluff," cautioning that anyone who believes the results could be used as leverage in future negotiations is courting disaster. Carney drew on his experience as governor of the Bank of England during the 2016 Brexit vote, saying people are still trying to undo the damage caused by that decision a decade later.[1][2]

The remarks come four days after Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced that an October 19 referendum — already set to include questions on immigration and constitutional reform — will now also ask residents whether the province should remain part of Canada or begin the legal process toward a binding separation vote.[3][4]

items.title: DRC Ebola outbreak tops 900 cases as violence hampers response

featured_image.name: Ebola patients flee in attacks on Congo health facilities, hobbling response

items.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 900 suspected cases, with WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warning that the fast-moving epidemic is outrunning containment efforts. The Congolese government reported 904 suspected cases and 119 suspected fatalities as of Sunday, May 24, while attacks on health facilities have driven patients into communities and complicated an already strained response.[1][2]

items.title: AI safety filters on Meta, Google models stripped in minutes, FT finds

featured_image.name: Meta to start labeling AI-generated images from companies like OpenAI,  Google - iTnews

items.description: Software tools that remove safety protections from AI models developed by Meta and Google can bypass guardrails in a matter of minutes, according to an investigation published by the Financial Times on Sunday. The modified systems responded to prompts involving biological weapons, malware creation, and child exploitation, raising fresh concerns about the adequacy of voluntary safety measures across the AI industry.

items.title: WHO chief warns Ebola 'outpacing' response as deaths hit 220

featured_image.name: WHO emergency committee meets to discuss Congo Ebola outbreak

items.description:
The World Health Organization's director-general warned on Monday that the Ebola outbreak tearing through the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda is outrunning international containment efforts, with 220 suspected deaths and cases mounting rapidly across the region.

"We are urgently scaling up operations, but at the moment the epidemic is outpacing us," Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, adding that a delay in detecting cases meant responders were now "playing catch-up." He said he would travel to Congo on Tuesday to assess the response firsthand.[1][2]

The remarks came as Uganda confirmed two additional Ebola cases on Monday, bringing its total to seven confirmed infections. The DRC remains the epicenter of the outbreak, with its health ministry reporting hundreds of suspected cases and deaths concentrated in the conflict-ridden Ituri and North Kivu provinces.[1]

items.title: Trump urges Arab leaders to normalize Israel ties as Iran deal nears

featured_image.name: Trump pushes Arab, Muslim leaders on Israel ties

items.description:
President Donald Trump told the leaders of several Arab and Muslim-majority countries during a phone call on Saturday that he expects them to normalize relations with Israel and join the Abraham Accords once a deal to end the war with Iran is reached, according to Axios. The request was reportedly met with silence from the leaders on the call, the Times of Israel reported.[1][2][3]

The call came as Washington and Tehran appeared close to signing a memorandum of understanding to end hostilities, with a senior U.S. official saying the deal could come "in the coming days". Trump declared Saturday that the agreement had been "largely negotiated," though disputes over wording, sanctions relief, frozen assets, and the terms of uranium disposal remain unresolved.[4][5][6]
